content.value_statement: Quantum projects need reliable patterns for circuits, hardware, chemistry, and training. This skill guides PennyLane workflows with focused examples and references.
actual_capabilities: Explains PennyLane installation and optional hardware plugins.
Shows quantum circuit construction with gates, measurements, and QNodes.
Guides hybrid quantum-classical models with PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow integration.
Covers VQE, QAOA, optimizers, gradients, and barren plateau guidance.
Documents simulator and hardware device selection across supported providers.
References templates, transforms, compilation, noise models, and resource estimation.
limitations: It is documentation guidance and does not execute circuits by itself.
Hardware access still requires provider accounts, credentials, and costs.
Examples may need updates for installed PennyLane and plugin versions.
It does not replace quantum algorithm validation or domain review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Quantum Circuits
use_cases.description: Design QNodes, measurements, and ansatz patterns before building a larger PennyLane project.

use_cases.title: Train Hybrid Models
use_cases.description: Plan data encoding, framework integration, and training loops for quantum machine learning experiments.

use_cases.title: Study Molecular Workflows
use_cases.description: Review VQE, molecular Hamiltonians, and chemistry ansatz choices for small simulation studies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Circuit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PennyLane skill to outline a simple two-qubit circuit with one expectation measurement.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PennyLane skill to compare simulator and hardware backend choices for a four-qubit experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Hybrid Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PennyLane skill to plan a hybrid classifier, including encoding, ansatz, optimizer, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a VQE Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PennyLane skill to improve a VQE workflow for convergence, gradient method, backend choice, and diagnostics.

output_examples.input: Plan a PennyLane experiment for a variational classifier.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow covering feature encoding, circuit layers, optimizer choice, validation metrics, and simulator-first testing.

output_examples.input: Compare PennyLane backends for a small chemistry simulation.
output_examples.output: A practical comparison of default simulators, hardware plugins, credential needs, expected costs, and recommended first steps.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow quantum optimization workflow.
output_examples.output: A focused checklist for gradient method, learning rate schedule, initialization, circuit depth, and backend performance choices.

best_practices: Start on local simulators before using paid quantum hardware.
Match gradient methods and optimizers to the chosen backend.
Track circuit depth, shots, costs, and convergence diagnostics.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode provider credentials in shared notebooks or scripts.
Do not assume simulator results transfer directly to noisy hardware.
Do not increase circuit depth without checking gradients and resources.

faq.question: Does this skill execute PennyLane code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for building PennyLane workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with quantum hardware?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains backend selection and plugins, but users manage accounts and credentials.

faq.question: Does it cover quantum machine learning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers hybrid models, data encoding, framework integration, and training patterns.

faq.question: Does it include quantum chemistry guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers VQE, molecular Hamiltonians, ansatz choices, and chemistry workflows.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users verify first?
faq.answer: Verify PennyLane versions, plugin compatibility, credentials, and backend costs before running experiments.
